significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling: a token's early-layer "convergence depth" and semantic role predict both its tolerance to removing later-layer computation and the resulting compute–accuracy tradeoff. This fixes expectations beyond individual tokens—"connectives, restatements, hedging, formatting" should converge earlier and be less causally dependent on late layers than "novel deductions, arithmetic results, sub-conclusions"—so it establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a causal account of which token roles consume depth. CALM (Schuster et al., NeurIPS 2022) and LayerSkip (Elhoushi et al., ACL 2024) demonstrate that reliable adaptive-depth signals affect practical inference decisions; a false result here would distinguishably rule out prediction stability and the proposed role taxonomy as reliable indicators of causal depth need, though not adaptive depth generally. Topic-substitution check: efficient interpretable reasoning alone would not imply this role-to-convergence-to-causal-necessity relation, so the score comes from the claim-specific coupling rather than the topic.

reach.justification: The named handles are the online "convergence layer" measurement and the "training-free per-token depth-allocation controller" that skips remaining layers once the prediction is stable. This is ex ante within each token: the signal is read before the remaining computation and permits an immediate inference-time action, with potential uptake by deployment and inference-system practitioners rather than only researchers analyzing completed failures. After per-model recalibration, the asserted qualitative relation still predicts that shallow-converged semantic classes will tolerate late-layer removal, although the claim provides no invariant numerical threshold and acknowledges that "convergence-depth thresholds may not transfer across models/datasets"; its stated scope nevertheless covers several model families and GSM8K, MATH, and ProntoQA-style tasks. Topic-substitution check: the broad topic supplies neither this measurable signal nor an actionable early-exit controller, so the reach is attributable to the specific handle.
